title: The Crushed Canvas
crime: During art class a heavy easel was slammed into a canvas, tearing it. Each student claimed how much work they did moving the easel, and one lied.
deed: you shoved the easel into the canvas, ripping it, then reported a false amount of work.
oath: My work on the easel was {value} {unit}. Check the board.
measure: The lab reads each student's applied force and the distance the easel moved from the sensor log.
hint: *Work equals force times distance. Multiply the two numbers you measured.
arrive: The art studio wall shows a shredded canvas. The Baron erased the law of work.
Three students. Each one told the teacher how much work they did moving the easel.
Question them, then check the sensor log.
inspect: Fingerprints on the easel handle and torn canvas indicate a push.
The sensor log lists force and displacement for each attempt. Work reveals the liar.
confession: Okay, I slammed the easel into the canvas and fudged my work number. The Baron said work couldn't be checked any more.
